v1_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled starting August 2026 and remains elevated through September (E-04), while the majority of disputed bills are based on ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutes (E-01) and no tariff/rate change occurred in the period (E-02). This evidence best supports that the surge is driven by a genuine rise in billed amounts ("bill shock", H-CONSUMPTION-SHOCK-NO-ERROR) rather than by estimate-substitution or tariff-driven billing errors, while ticket-handling speed itself remains within SLA (E-03), so the surge is a volume problem, not a response-time or bill-defect problem.
v2_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep) and remains elevated (E-04). For the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-01), 1,184 had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read that was nonetheless rejected on billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12); this is best explained by rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw register value against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), against meter firmware v4.2 (rolled out June 2026, the rejected reads' firmware) which reports register values in units of 0.1 m3 (E-14) — so a legitimate read is misclassified as high-consumption, rejected, and estimate-substituted into an incorrect bill the customer disputes. This confirmed mechanism accounts for the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputes; whether the same unit-mismatch defect also explains the billed-amount increases behind the larger ACTUAL-read-dominant share of disputes (1,785 of E-01) is not yet established.
